title: Side panel vs centered modal
prompt: Build a panel that slides in from the right edge of the screen so a user can edit a list of filters without leaving the current page. Keep the main content visible behind it.
differences: A1 tends to use a centered Dialog that blocks the whole page
A4 uses a Sheet that slides from the edge, main content still visible
The screen layout is fundamentally different, not just styled differently

title: Rich data grid vs plain table
prompt: Render a list of 500 workers with columns for name, role, and site. Users need to sort by any column, filter by name, and page through the results.
differences: A1 tends to render a plain static table
A4 uses DataTable: sortable column headers, a filter input, pagination controls
A4 shows interactive chrome the baseline simply does not have

title: Transient toast vs inline alert
prompt: After a user saves their settings, show a brief confirmation that auto-dismisses after a few seconds and does not take up permanent space on the page. Include whatever app-root wiring is needed for it to appear.
differences: A1 tends to use a permanent inline Alert that occupies page space
A4 uses a floating toast that auto-dismisses (with the required Toaster at the root)
Best seen as a 2-frame / short capture: appears, then fades

title: Multi-step form workflow
prompt: Build a guided 'create project' flow split into three steps: first the project's basic details, then its team members, then a final review of everything entered. Show the user's progress through the steps, validate each step before advancing, and let the user move back and forward between steps.
differences: A1 tends to render one long flat form
A4 uses a Stepper with a progress indicator, sectioned steps, and inline validation
A4 adds wayfinding (back/next, step state) the baseline lacks

title: Destructive action emphasis
prompt: Add a button that permanently deletes the selected record. Make its visual treatment communicate that the action is dangerous and irreversible.
differences: A1 tends to render a neutral / default button
Smallest change, crispest read: a clean emphasis/color difference
